title: Stabilize sub-minute metering to prevent floating invoice lines and duplicate export artifacts
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem:
Several customers have reported invoice line volatility where lines appear, disappear, or shift amounts between hourly exports and NetSuite import. Root causes: (1) sub-minute usage bursts (rate-limit retries, client backoff storms) cause interleaved usage pulses that the hourly aggregator mis-buckets; (2) non-deterministic export ordering leads to duplicate or split line items when the export consumer (Stripe/Netsuite reconciler) replays or partially ingests lines; (3) simplistic mid-cycle proration that rounds at minute granularity loses fractions across plan swaps.

Goals:
- Make aggregate usage bucketing deterministic down to the second so short-lived pulses are always assigned consistently.
- Ensure export lines are idempotent and mergeable to avoid orphaned partial invoice lines after retries or multi-run exports.
- Improve proration allocation accuracy for plan swaps that occur within an hour by allocating using per-second overlap instead of coarse minute rounding.

Design summary:
1) Second-anchored aggregation: change hourly rollup to epoch-second anchoring per customer/timezone. Aggregation keys will include (account_id, product_id, bucket_start_epoch_sec). This avoids shifting when delayed events arrive within the same second window.

2) Deterministic export sequencing & fingerprinting: each export line will include an export_fingerprint = sha256(account_id || bucket_start_epoch_sec || product_id || feature_flags || quantized_usage) and an export_seq (monotonic per-export-run). Exports are sorted by (account_id, bucket_start_epoch_sec, export_fingerprint) before emission. Consumers will dedupe by fingerprint + export_run_id.

3) Idempotent ingest tokens: when writing invoices to Stripe we will attach metadata.invoice_export_token = export_run_id:export_fingerprint so downstream imports can be retried safely.

4) Near-duplicate collapsing heuristics: add a reconciliation stage that merges export lines for the same (account_id, product_id) with bucket_start within +/- 2 seconds and total quantity difference < 0.5% using volume-weighted averaging. This prevents micro-split lines from creating multiple invoice rows.

5) Per-second proration for plan swaps: compute prorated quantity/price as proportion of seconds in billing segment, carry fractional cents to an accumulator per-account to ensure deterministic rounding and preserve total billed amount across swaps.

6) Backfill & migration plan: implement a readonly shadow export mode where the new aggregator writes shadow export files to s3/prefix=shadow-agg/ for 48h and compare diffs with legacy exports. Then run a controlled backfill for customers with known drift using a migration script (backfill_window param) and produce repair adjustments.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for new fingerprint generation, deterministic sorting, and per-second proration math.
- Integration test suite that replays historical telemetry with injected retry storms to assert stable export fingerprints and no duplicate invoice lines.
- Fuzz harness (existing nightly job) to simulate 0-1000ms jitter, rate-limit retries at 10-60s, and heavy burst patterns.
- Shadow-run comparison dashboards: export_line_count, exported_total_tokens, export_duplication_rate, invoice_delta_amounts.

Operational concerns:
- Performance: moving to second bucketing increases cardinality; plan to shard aggregators by account_id hash and keep memory window fixed. Expect ~8% CPU increase on aggregator fleet during peak; measured in canary runs.
- Storage: fingerprint indexing will add ~40 bytes per export line. Use compressed export manifests.
- Rollback: can stop emitting production exports and flip back to legacy aggregator; however, partially-applied backfills are harder to revert — backfills will be gated by manual approval.

Runbook (high level):
1) If export_duplication_rate spikes > 0.5% after deploy, toggle export_run_mode=legacy and notify billing-oncall.
2) If invoice delta total across top-10 customers > $500, pause backfill and open incident.
3) For late-arriving events causing re-aggregation, we accept re-export with same fingerprint so downstream dedupe prevents duplicate invoice lines.

Deliverables:
- Code changes to aggregator service (agg-service) + export writer (exportor) + reconciler worker.
- Backfill script: tools/billing/backfill_prorate_repair.py
- Dashboard and alert rules in Grafana/Alertmanager.
- PRD and migration playbook linked in comments.

Risks:
- Edge-case: customers with highly variable timezones may still see friction; mitigated by anchoring to account-configured timezone and providing a per-account flag to use legacy minute bucketing.
- Finance reconciliation must sign off on fractional-cent accumulator behavior.

Success criteria:
- Duplicate export lines reduced to <0.1% in canary customers.
- Invoice total variance vs legacy < 0.2% for a 7-day window post-migration.
- No customer-facing invoice regressions reported within 30 days of rollout.
